_description: Standing macro/geopolitical situations referenced across briefings. Loader: scripts/generate_daily.py:load_ongoing_situations(). Manually maintained. Set status to 'resolved' when a situation is no longer relevant; the loader will skip it. Add new situations when they enter the briefing rotation. Keep facts list under 6 items per situation (loader caps at 6). Anchor phrase is the one-clause framing used on FIRST reference each week per Rule 18.

iran_hormuz.anchor: the Iran-Hormuz cycle — a July re-escalation (vessels hit, tankers reversing, crude running) that has since cooled, with the premium deflating again into August
facts: the situation re-escalated in early-to-mid July: commercial vessels hit, tanker traffic reversed course, and crude ran multi-percent sessions on Iran headlines
by late July the market's focus shifted from Hormuz risk to Red Sea/Houthi rerouting costs — two offsetting freight stories
as of Aug 3 the briefing's own read: crude supply building, Hormuz premium still deflating, no input-cost surprise
the premium has built and unwound twice since April — treat fresh escalation headlines as a known pattern, not a new regime
diesel tightness, not crude, has been the input-cost story for fall fieldwork

china_trade_deal.anchor: China's $17 billion annual US ag purchase commitment (May 18 deal, through 2028), now showing up as periodic confirmed soybean sales
facts: confirmed China soybean purchases have repeatedly lifted beans intraday in July, with a buy-the-rumor-sell-the-fact pattern capping follow-through
the commitment spans beans, beef, and poultry beyond prior soybean levels
beans set 52-week highs in late July with Chinese demand as one leg of the story (heat premium was the other)
US soybeans still face roughly 13% at the Chinese border (3% MFN + 10% retaliatory levy) — the truce holds through Nov 10, 2026
purchases have supported the board without producing a sustained trend on their own

cargill_fort_morgan_lockout.anchor: the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity
facts: 1,700 workers were still locked out as of the end of July, the last confirmation on file — if today's news has an update, prefer it and say so.
Roughly 6,000 head/day of processing capacity remains removed on that last confirmation.
The dynamic is processing-constrained, not supply-constrained: packer margins, not cattle numbers, are the binding constraint.

growing_season_2026.anchor: the 2026 growing season: USDA's first survey-based yields (Aug 12) came in BELOW trade expectations on both crops while acreage went up, with Pro Farmer's crop tour Aug 17-20 the next real test
facts: USDA's August WASDE printed Aug 12: corn yield 180.7 bu/acre (down 2.3 from July's 183.0) and soybeans 52.7 (down 0.3 from 53.0). These are USDA's CURRENT numbers — 183.0/53.0 are superseded and must never be quoted as current.

Acres offset the yield cut: corn planted up 1.4M to 96.7M and soybeans up 1.4M to 86.8M, so production is 16.013B bu of corn and a record 4.519B bu of soybeans. Corn 2026/27 carryout fell to 1.653B (from 1.79B); soybean carryout rose to 320M.
The market traded the yield cut, not the big crop: December corn settled up 15 cents at $4.78 on report day (Tuesday's close was $4.63).
Pro Farmer's crop tour runs Aug 17-20 with the national number Friday Aug 21. The scouts have NOT been in the field yet as of Aug 15 — do not narrate tour results before they exist.

AGSIST's own nowcast reads corn 183.6 / beans 53.8 (locked Aug 11, week ending Aug 9) — now ABOVE USDA on both. Our two locked directional calls (corn up, beans up) were graded WRONG on Aug 12; USDA revised down. The miss is on the record and should be owned, not hidden.

cattle_mexico_screwworm.anchor: the screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports, with the first phased port reopening set for Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ
facts: The border closure has tightened feeder supply all summer and is one leg of the historic feeder rally.
USDA confirmed a phased reopening starting Aug 24 at Douglas, AZ — still UPCOMING as of Aug 15; do not describe ports as reopened.
Feeders broke roughly 3% in late July as the market began pricing returning supply rather than scarcity.
The feeder/live spread is the tell as the Aug 24 date approaches.
Screwworm spread beyond Texas earlier in the season; containment progress drives the reopening pace.

farm_bill_2026.anchor: the 2026 Farm Bill endgame: the Senate Ag markup FAILED on party lines Aug 6, pushing a revote to September against the Sep 30 extension deadline
facts: Senate Ag Committee markup FAILED Aug 6 on a party-line vote over the SNAP state cost-share dispute. It did not pass — a revote is expected in September. Never describe the bill as having cleared committee.
The House passed H.R. 7567 in April; the Senate's Aug 1 revised text added year-round E15 sales, a structural corn-demand tailwind if it is ever enacted.
The Aug 1 text delays the SNAP state cost-share to FY2029 (FY2031 for high-error states), aimed at Democratic holdouts. It has not been CBO-scored.
A separate $15-17B economic-aid push sits outside the bill; no program details exist yet.
The current extension expires Sep 30, 2026 — the hard date for a bill or another extension.
